scope: M154 RTL/SVA/TB, exact-SHA sealed VCS/DC receipts and runners, M150/M152 correction overlay and reviews, fresh exact production VCS/DC replay, exhaustive bank/address/order/context/fault/backpressure VCS, and output-register optimization assessment.

score.disposition: GO for the standalone four-independent-vector identity supplier under the frozen output-holding synchronous macro model. The M150/M152 single-vector identity P0 is closed at this interface. NO-GO for the 1.805357581x cycle ratio, physical/system speedup, paper PPA or headline use until the real macros, load schedule, four-bank accumulator and signed numeric replay are integrated.

independent_vcs_hammer.legal_descriptor_definition: Every conflict-free ordered destination tuple for prefix sizes one through four across all 16 sources: 16 * (8 + 48 + 192 + 384).
independent_vcs_hammer.same_bank_attack_definition: All 16 ordered destination pairs sharing destination[1:0], plus one fault with both elastic slots occupied.

macro_output_hold_sensitivity.negative_test: Toggle every bank output on each disabled-read edge instead of holding it.
macro_output_hold_sensitivity.interpretation: The second elastic slot stores only request metadata; its 3072-bit response remains on the external macro outputs until result capacity opens. Correctness therefore requires output hold/clock-enable semantics or an explicit response capture.

resident_capacity_accounting.correct_interpretation: 98,304 bits is an external interface capacity requirement, not synthesized resident SRAM evidence. The 13,282.668059 um2 number prices only standard-cell control/tag/data-buffer logic.

required_contracts: Each bank output holds its last synchronous response while read enable is low.
The token/address metadata remains aligned with all four bank outputs.
descriptor_ready directly propagates result backpressure before another macro read overwrites held data.
macro_output_token.tradeoff: A one-token design removes the 3072-bit result FF but reduces the current maximum in-flight depth from two transactions to one during stalls. Keeping two entries requires reread/replay or another wide storage element.

fused_accumulator.reason: Consume the four 768-bit macro outputs directly into four conflict-free signed accumulator banks. This removes the external wide result buffer while implementing the M152 accumulator path that currently blocks speedup admission.
required_features: four banked read-modify-write or equivalent update paths
same-address forwarding and exact overflow proof
mask-aware tails, context/fault atomicity and real checkpoint numeric replay
bound accumulator macros and load/commit recurrence

m155_interface_impact.workspace_snapshot: Read-only inspection found rtl_m155, tb_m155 and verif_m155 sources, but no M155 contract or sealed RUN_COMPLETE receipt. Their behavior is therefore not admitted by this M154 review.

interface_alignment.destination_tuple_mask: Both interfaces use four tuple positions and the same legal prefix masks 0001/0011/0111/1111.
interface_alignment.bank_conflict_rule: Both reject simultaneous destinations with equal destination[1:0].
interface_alignment.row_and_destination: M154 result_row[8:0] and result_destination[2:0] match the observed M155 update_row and update_destination geometry.
interface_alignment.negate: M154 result_negate maps directly to the observed M155 update_negate.
interface_alignment.vector_width_adapter: M154 emits signed INT8; the observed M155 input is signed11. An explicit bit-exact sign extension {{3{result_vector[7]}}, result_vector} is required before M155 performs its signed12 negate.
interface_alignment.context_adapter: M154 carries sequence/operator/partition and context open/close; the observed M155 window start/end interface carries no identity. A wrapper must atomically bind one M154 context to one M155 window, forbid cross-context update acceptance, and order close/end/fault drain without losing older accepted work.

p1_effects.condition: If the 3,072-bit result register is replaced by a macro-output token, M155 backpressure can hold M154's response while its pending macro output is live.
p1_effects.required_closure: Bind output-holding SRAM semantics or implement response capture/re-read before connecting result_ready to M155 update_ready.

p1_effects.condition: The signed-width adapter and identity-less M155 window boundary are not frozen or sealed.
p1_effects.required_closure: Seal a wrapper with signed8-to-signed11 replay, context/window identity assertions, and end/fault atomicity tests before admitting the fused path.

remaining_closure.external_weight_sram: Open: M154 exposes four banks but instantiates no SRAM macro.
remaining_closure.weight_loading: Open: no checkpoint payload load RTL, contents receipt, source-key switch or load-to-use schedule is present.
remaining_closure.weight_macro_timing_energy: Open: no selected macro DB, read-enable/output-hold characterization, macro STA or macro power evidence is bound.
remaining_closure.accumulator_logic: In progress only: an unsealed M155 RTL/TB/SVA snapshot exists; this review does not admit it.
remaining_closure.accumulator_sram_and_commit: Open: no bound accumulator macro, physical RMW timing/energy, full commit/drain path or real-trace cycle seal is present.
remaining_closure.signed_numeric_replay: Open: no end-to-end checkpoint-derived M154-to-M155 lane replay is sealed.

findings.title: Two-entry correctness depends on an unbound external-macro output-hold contract
findings.evidence: When the result slot is stalled and the request slot holds the next transaction, M154 delays sampling bank_rd_data until result capacity opens. The frozen behavioral SRAM retains outputs while rd_en=0. An independent negative sensitivity that toggles disabled bank outputs produces a vector mismatch at 52.5 ns.
findings.impact: A selected macro whose output is not held or clock-enabled can corrupt the pending second transaction even though RTL/SVA pass against the behavioral model.
findings.required_action: Bind an exact macro with output-hold semantics and timing, assert response stability while request_valid_q is blocked, or capture/replay the pending response explicitly.

findings.title: M154 closes vector identity only; the sealed M155 integration and 1.805357581x execution path are still absent
findings.evidence: The 98,304-bit store is external, weight loading and real checkpoint replay are absent, and no sealed four-bank accumulator/RMW/forwarding path exists. The observed unsealed M155 snapshot accepts signed11 vectors and identity-less window boundaries, whereas M154 emits signed8 vectors with sequence/operator/partition contexts. The frozen M150/M152 correction requires these boundaries and all physical storage paths before hardware speedup admission.
findings.impact: Four correct vector reads do not prove four signed accumulator updates per cycle, macro bandwidth/energy, source-key switch cost or executable recurrence. Without a bit-exact width/context/fault adapter, even the observed M155 source is not an admitted M154 endpoint. The 1.805357581x value remains an opportunity bound.
findings.required_action: Integrate exact SRAMs and loading with a sealed four-bank fused accumulator; add explicit signed8-to-signed11 extension and atomic context/window/fault binding; replay signed checkpoint updates; and rerun accepted-cycle recurrence with stalls and source-key switches.

findings.title: The 3,072-bit result register dominates the logic-only island
findings.evidence: 3,072 of 3,273 sequential cells are payload bits (93.86%). They occupy 6,193.152 um2, 46.63% of total DC area. The mapped reference histogram also contains 6,147 AOI22 plus 3,072 OAI211 cells consistent with the wide hold/select cone.
findings.impact: The standalone supplier pays a large standard-cell buffering cost immediately before an as-yet-unimplemented accumulator, weakening area/energy competitiveness.
findings.required_action: Prefer a fused accumulator. A macro-output token is also feasible if output hold is bound, but it reduces stall-time in-flight depth from two to one and requires recurrence replay. Do not cite the inferred 90.35% cone as measured area recovery without a matched A/B DC run.

findings.title: Production VCS is reproducible but narrow
findings.evidence: The sealed regression uses 55 descriptors and three attacks. The independent test exercises 10,112 exhaustive legal descriptors, every bank/address and tuple order, all 12 invalid masks, all 16 same-bank pairs, three context mismatches, three API collisions, two occupied elastic slots and reset cancellation.
findings.impact: The sealed PASS alone does not show full partition closure even though the independent result supports the implementation.
findings.required_action: Promote the exhaustive address/order, two-slot fault atomicity and macro-response-hold assertions into the repaired exact-SHA production regression.

findings.title: No RTL-to-mapped-netlist Formality receipt is present
findings.evidence: Fresh RTL VCS and DC mapping reproduce and mapped Verilog/SDC/DDC/SVF exist, but no M154 Formality seal was found.
findings.impact: The mapped QoR point is not yet functionally tied to the RTL by commercial equivalence proof.
findings.required_action: Run exact-identity Formality on the chosen token/fused revision before physical admission.

findings.title: DC is zero-macro, ideal-clock and prephysical
findings.evidence: Fresh DC exactly reproduces 13,282.668059 um2, 10 levels, +1.6514 ns setup and +0.0002 ns hold at 3 ns, but instantiates zero of the four 32x768 SRAM banks and uses ZeroWireload with no routed clock, SAIF or PTPX.
findings.impact: Neither the 98,304-bit resident storage nor macro timing/energy is included, and the very small DC hold margin is not routed hold closure.
findings.required_action: Keep this as supplier standard-cell evidence only; bind SRAM/accumulator macros and run propagated-clock STA and activity-based power for paper PPA.

validated_strengths: M154 supplies four independent destination-owned vectors and therefore repairs the M150/M152 single-vector multicast identity P0 at its standalone interface.
Bank selection destination[1:0], address {destination[2], source}, tuple order and invalid-tail zeroing pass exhaustive independent VCS.
The one-cycle synchronous response pipeline sustains II=1 under ready operation and reaches two in-flight transactions under backpressure.
A younger protocol fault does not erase either an older held result or the older pending request behind it; both drain after sticky quarantine.
Sequence/operator/partition tags, all invalid masks, same-bank conflicts, API collisions and reset cancellation behave fail-closed under the frozen macro model.
Sealed manifests verify and fresh exact production VCS/DC replays reproduce the stated evidence.

admitted: Standalone four-bank identity-correct vector supplier under a one-cycle synchronous output-holding external macro model
Conflict-free bank/address routing, tuple order, context metadata, two-entry elastic backpressure and fault-atomic drain
M150 single-vector identity P0 closure at the M154 interface
Flattened TSMC28 standard-cell-only control/tag/3072-bit-result-buffer area and ideal-clock timing at 3 ns
not_admitted: Physical 98,304-bit resident SRAM implementation, area, latency or energy
Weight loading or real checkpoint vector replay
Four-bank signed accumulator RMW, forwarding or commit
Measured area recovery from macro-output token or fused accumulator
Physical/system speedup, paper PPA, DATE headline or best-paper readiness
